findings.F1: The tested relation is real and stands out. In rising months (30-day return above 0), the slope of the demeaned next-7-day return on the 7-day return is 0.142 with t 4.35 over 893 grid cases. The top r7 quintile earns +3.5% over the coin's average (t 3.21, n 252) and the bottom quintile earns −0.9%. In falling months the slope turns negative (−0.057, t −1.49, n 830).
findings.F2: Nearness to the 30-day high carries no information beyond the 7-day return. In rising months, with r7 and the distance to the 30-day high in one regression, r7 keeps t 3.91 and the distance to the high falls to t 0.11 (n 893). The anchoring-to-the-high reading adds nothing over plain one-week momentum.
findings.F3: In falling months the 30-day return reverses. The slope of the demeaned next-7-day return on r30 is −0.074 (t −2.35, n 830), so a deeper monthly fall is followed by a higher next week. The slope is negative in 5 of 6 coins (BTC t −2.85, n 126). It is stronger in 2018–2021 (t −2.35, n 425) than in 2022–2025 (t −0.88, n 405).
findings.F4: A one-day fall large relative to the coin's 20-day daily volatility is followed by a higher next-day return. The pooled slope of the demeaned next-day return on the volatility-scaled down move is −0.0031 (t −3.61, n 7151). The slope is negative in all 6 coins (XMR t −3.21, XRP t −2.08). Day-averaged across coins, falls of 1 to 2 volatilities are followed by +0.63% (t 1.82) in 2018–2021 and +0.12% (t 0.53) in 2022–2025, so the effect has weakened lately.
findings.F5: A 3-day rise continues and a 3-day fall does not reverse. On the non-overlapping 3-day grid, the slope of the demeaned next-3-day return on the volatility-scaled 3-day rise is 0.0070 (t 2.89, n 2356). For 3-day falls it is −0.0013 (t −0.46, n 2359).
findings.F6: The rising-month momentum holds at every volatility level. The r7 slope is t 2.48 in the low tercile, t 1.43 in the middle and t 3.18 in the high tercile (about 297 cases each). Scaling r7 by volatility gives t 3.61, so the effect is not a volatility artefact.
findings.F7: Weekday effects do not stand out once coins are averaged per day. The best day is Friday, at +0.32% with t 2.17 across 414 days, out of 7 weekdays tested. Its t is 1.70 in 2018–2021 and 1.37 in 2022–2025. I count this as chance.

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day return is negative, the deeper its 30-day fall, the higher its return over the next 7 days.
ideas.consequence: In a falling month, a coin's steepest monthly declines are a reason to look for a long rebound rather than to stay out, which the current strategy does.
ideas.name: falling-month depth rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its own 20-day daily volatility, the higher its return over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp one-day drop measured against the coin's usual daily swing is a reason to buy for a one-day bounce rather than to sell into it.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled down-day bounce

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 3-day rise relative to its own 20-day daily volatility, the higher its return over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A strong 3-day advance, scaled by the coin's volatility, is a reason to hold or add to a long over the following 3 days.
ideas.name: short-horizon rise continuation
